source: Huang et al. (2023) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without external feedback, models fail to fix their own reasoning answers. Sometimes accuracy drops after a self-correction round.
quote: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback
limits: Reasoning tasks only; intrinsic correction (no oracle). Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Practice by self-critique alone is not deliberate practice: it lacks a reliable error signal. Gate revisions on external checks (tests, solver).

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes?
finding: Survey finds no prior work showing successful self-correction from prompted LLM feedback, except on tasks suited to it. Reliable external feedback and large-scale fine-tuning do work.
numbers: No figures in abstract. TACL vol 12, pp 1417-1440.
limits: Critiques earlier studies for unfair evaluation setups. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Parallel to the human finding: practice helps where feedback is clear and objective (games, music), weakly elsewhere. Same boundary for the agent.

source: Kumar et al. (2024) Training Language Models to Self-Correct via RL (SCoRe)
finding: Self-correction is largely ineffective in modern LLMs. Offline SFT on correction traces fails (distribution mismatch, collapse). Online multi-turn RL on self-generated data fixes part of it.
numbers: Gains of 15.6% (MATH) and 9.1% (HumanEval) on Gemini 1.0 Pro / 1.5 Flash; pairing ambiguous in abstract.
limits: Needs weight training; not a prompt-only scaffold. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Practice that transfers needs training on the model's own error distribution, not on others' traces. A scaffold cannot copy this; it can only add verifiers.

source: Olausson et al. (2023) Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?
finding: Self-repair gains are often modest, vary by data subset, and are sometimes absent once repair cost is counted. The limit is the quality of the model's own feedback.
numbers: Code Llama, GPT-3.5, GPT-4 on HumanEval and APPS. Stronger-model feedback gave substantially larger gains. Human feedback to GPT-4 beat self-feedback.
quote: performance gains are often modest, vary a lot between subsets of the data
limits: Cost-normalised comparison. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Mirrors small deliberate-practice effects in professions: more repetitions give little when feedback quality is the bottleneck. Spend budget on better critics, not more rounds.

source: Stechly, Marquez, Kambhampati (2023) GPT-4 Doesn't Know It's Wrong
finding: On graph colouring GPT-4 is poor at verifying its own solutions, so self-critique loops do not help. Iteration gains come from the right answer being in top-k completions that an external verifier picks out.
numbers: No numbers in abstract. Task: graph colouring (NP-complete).
quote: call into question claims about the self-critiquing capabilities
limits: One task family. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Iterated practice acts as sampling plus a verifier, not as learning. Use a sound external verifier or do not loop.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine
finding: Same model gives feedback on its own output and refines it, with no training. Reported gain about 20% absolute on average over one-step generation.
numbers: 7 tasks; GPT-3.5, ChatGPT, GPT-4; ~20% absolute average gain.
limits: Later work (Huang 2023; Kamoi 2024) argues weak baselines inflate such gains. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: A cheap in-context practice loop works on tasks where the model can judge quality (style, dialogue). Contested on reasoning.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: Agents store verbal reflections on task feedback in an episodic memory and retry, with no weight updates. HumanEval pass@1 91% versus 80% for GPT-4.
numbers: 91% vs 80% pass@1 on HumanEval; gains across decision-making, coding, reasoning.
limits: Depends on a feedback signal (tests or scalar reward) being available. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Closest agent-loop analogue of deliberate practice: attempt, get feedback, reflect, retry. Works when feedback is objective.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager
finding: LLM agent in Minecraft with automatic curriculum, a growing skill library of code, and iterative prompting from errors. Skills transfer to a new world.
numbers: 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA.
limits: Single game; GPT-4 black-box. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Curriculum plus stored skills mirrors deliberate-practice design (stretch tasks, retained skills). Transfer shown only inside one domain.

source: Zelikman et al. (2022) STaR
finding: Loop: generate rationales, retry with hint when wrong, fine-tune on those that reach the correct answer, repeat. Comparable to a 30x larger model on CommonsenseQA.
numbers: 30x size equivalence on CommonsenseQA; other numbers not on abstract page.
limits: Needs ground-truth answers; weight updates. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Practice transfer needs verifiable answers. Filter by correct outcome, not by effort spent.

source: An et al. (2023) Learning From Mistakes Makes LLM Better Reasoner (LEMA)
finding: Fine-tuning on mistake plus GPT-4 correction pairs improves over CoT-only fine-tuning. Correction data and CoT data contribute differently.
limits: A stronger model acts as corrector, i.e. a coach. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Human deliberate practice relies on a coach. Here the coach is a stronger model. Without a coach the loop weakens (see Kamoi).

source: Chen et al. (2024) Self-Play Fine-Tuning (SPIN)
finding: Model plays against its previous iteration to tell its outputs from human data. Improves Open LLM Leaderboard, MT-Bench, BIG-Bench and beats DPO with extra GPT-4 preferences.
limits: Theory: optimum reached when policy matches the human data distribution, so a ceiling exists. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Self-practice has a ceiling set by the reference data, like practice saturating near elite level.

source: Yuan et al. (2024) Self-Rewarding Language Models
finding: Model judges its own outputs for iterative DPO. Three iterations on Llama 2 70B beat Claude 2, Gemini Pro and GPT-4 0613 on AlpacaEval 2.0.
limits: Judge quality is the limit. No score on page. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Self-judged practice can help on open-ended instruction tasks where model judgment is decent. Contrast with failures on reasoning.

source: Bai et al. (2022) Constitutional AI
finding: Critique-and-revise by the model against written principles, then RL from AI feedback. Cuts human labels needed.
limits: Fits value-laden tasks with a written rubric. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: A rubric acts as a coach substitute. Explicit criteria make self-critique usable.

source: Zhao et al. (2025) Absolute Zero
finding: One model proposes its own tasks to maximise learning progress and solves them, with a code executor as verifiable reward. Claims SOTA coding and math versus zero-setting models using tens of thousands of human examples.
limits: Only verifiable domains (code). Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Self-set stretch tasks (a deliberate-practice ingredient) work when an executor gives exact feedback.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1
finding: Pure RL with verifiable rewards elicits self-reflection, verification and strategy adaptation; beats SFT on human demonstrations on maths, coding, STEM.
numbers: No scores on abstract page. Nature 645:633-638.
limits: Verifiable tasks only. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Large practice volume with exact reward yields gains in domains like humans' games and music. Same boundary as Macnamara 2014.

source: Yue et al. (2025) Does RL Really Incentivize Reasoning Beyond the Base Model?
finding: RLVR models win at small k but base models have higher pass@k at large k. Reasoning ability appears bounded by the base model; distillation can add new patterns.
numbers: 6 RLVR algorithms compared; k=1 vs large k; no scores on page.
quote: does not elicit fundamentally new reasoning patterns
limits: Evidence from pass@k, not human-style transfer tests. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Practice sharpens sampling of what is already there, not new capacity. Parallels the near-zero gain of practice among elite performers.

source: Shumailov et al. (2023) The Curse of Recursion
finding: Training on model-generated data causes model collapse: tails of the distribution vanish. Seen in VAEs, GMMs and LLMs.
limits: Pure synthetic recursion; mixing real data reduces it. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Unverified self-practice can degrade. Keep external ground truth in the loop.

source: Villalobos et al. (2022) Will we run out of data?
finding: Public human text stock will be matched by training set size between 2026 and 2032 if trends continue. Synthetic data and data efficiency named as ways forward.
limits: Forecast, not measured behaviour. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Context for why self-generated practice is attractive and why its limits matter.

source: Ruoss et al. (2024) Amortized Planning with Large-Scale Transformers: Chess
finding: Transformer trained by supervised learning on 15B Stockfish-annotated points plays without search at Lichess blitz Elo 2895. Perfect distillation of search is not reached.
numbers: 10M games, 15B data points, up to 270M parameters, Elo 2895 vs humans.
limits: Games are where Macnamara found practice explains most variance (26%); data volume, not self-reflection. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Chess is the domain where practice-like volume pays most. Machine-side evidence for that boundary.

source: Schut et al. (2023) Bridging the Human-AI Knowledge Gap (AlphaZero)
finding: Concepts extracted from AlphaZero were teachable: 4 grandmasters improved on concept prototype positions.
numbers: 4 grandmasters; no numbers on abstract page.
limits: Tiny sample. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Machine-found knowledge can be passed to human experts. In reverse, coaching content could be used on agents.

source: Wang et al. (2022) Adversarial Policies Beat Superhuman Go AIs
finding: Adversaries win over 97% against KataGo at superhuman settings without playing good Go; attack survives adversarial training and human experts can use it.
numbers: Win rate >97% vs KataGo; zero-shot transfer to other Go AIs.
quote: Our adversaries do not win by playing Go well
limits: Go only. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Huge practice volume does not give robustness outside the practised distribution. Same non-transfer message as the human literature.

source: Huang et al. (2023) reading across to human split
finding: Pattern across the paper: self-correction helps when an external signal exists, is flat or hurts otherwise. This matches the human split between rule-bound domains and professions.
limits: The analogy is mine, not tested in the paper. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Design rule: add a practice loop only where the verifier is external; skip it for open-ended judgement.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) checklist for self-correction experiments
finding: Authors give a checklist and categorisation of research questions, and say many published gains used impractical frameworks or unfair comparisons.
limits: Survey, not a new experiment. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Test our own scaffold against same-budget baselines (best-of-N) before claiming practice-like gains.

source: Kumar et al. (2024) SCoRe mechanism
finding: Two-stage RL: first stage prevents collapse into making no changes, second adds a reward bonus for real corrections. Behaviour collapse is the failure of naive practice.
limits: Needs training. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: A prompt-level scaffold should detect no-op revisions (same answer returned) and count them as failure.

source: Olausson et al. (2023) feedback-quality finding
finding: Replacing the model's own feedback with a stronger model's feedback raised repair gains substantially.
limits: Code only. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Coach quality, not repetition count, moves results. Route critique to a different or stronger model if possible.

source: Yue et al. (2025) distillation vs RLVR
finding: Distillation from a teacher added new reasoning patterns where RLVR did not.
limits: One benchmark family. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Learning from a better teacher beats solo practice, echoing the coach role in the human deliberate practice account.

source: Zhao et al. (2025) Absolute Zero as self-set curriculum
finding: Task proposer is rewarded for tasks at the edge of its ability (learning progress), an automated version of stretch goals.
limits: Code executor only. Only the arXiv abstract page was read, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: If a verifier exists, an agent can generate its own graded practice items.
